newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CLARKE AND BEST UNDERMINE ROWELL PLANS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CLARKE AND BEST UNDERMINE ROWELL PLANS.

text.p: England back-row forward Ben Clarke has been ruled out of the England team to face Italy at Twickenham on Saturday with a leg injury.
He will be replaced by Wasps' Chris Sheasby, the fifth new cap in the England side, the most they have fielded for 11 years.
"I am very close to being fully fit, but to play international rugby you have got to be 100 per cent," said Clarke.

England coach Jack Rowell has also been hit by a savage attack from his predecessor Dick Best, who has predicted in an interview with Rugby News magazine that Rowell will be sacked by the end of the season.
"I don't think he will be either coach or manager by the time of the next World Cup in 1999," said Best, critical of Rowell's decision to stick with older players.
"I think bringing back people like Dean Richards wasted a whole year in the development of the England team. Rowell did it to get a result, otherwise he would have been out of a job."

Rugby Football Union officials, some of whom have been described as "two-faced and gutless" by Best, immediately defended Rowell, who supervised a grand slam in 1995 and a Five Nations Championship triumph last winter.
The coach himself shrugged off Best's comments.
"It is not my practice to comment or criticise on the work of other coaches," he said.
"I do not understand the motives of people who seek to disrupt the preparations of the national team."
